subject: Pilot buffer policy and temporary burst-lane coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot buffer policy and temporary burst-lane coordination

Team / Nimbus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed, Nimbus Health is planning a 6-week pilot starting March 8 that will exercise model-heavy inference patterns (short chat sessions, high concurrency). To avoid noisy throttling on their Dedicated pool and to keep latency predictable, we want to propose a short-lived "pilot buffer" and a controlled burst-lane for the pilot window.

High-level proposal (attached: pilot_capacity_plan.xlsx):
- Reserved pilot buffer: 12 vGPU-equivalent slots (2 weeks baseline, adjustable)
- Temporary burst-lane: additional 8 slots for scheduled peak windows (auto-evict at end of pilot day)
- Autoscale exception: allow burst-lane to spin above normal per-tenant limits only for the pilot time window and under a soft SLO of 99th pct latency fallback to alternative region/model.

Ask: Can infra sign off on the feasibility and the ops runbook required for quick eviction and billing attribution? Legal/procurement (Nimbus) — would a pilot carveout like this work for your team from a procurement/contracting viewpoint?

We want concrete next steps by EOD Tuesday so we can lock infra changes and send a short amendment to Nimbus procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot buffer policy and temporary burst-lane coordination

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Two quick product/ops clarifications: 

1) Autoscale exception surface: are we asking to bypass per-tenant max_instances or to create an alternative burst pool that is pre-wired to the same model family? The latter is simpler from isolation/billing.
2) Eviction policy: for Nimbus's use-case I recommend a deterministic FIFO eviction that first drains non-committed batch requests — we should capture that in the runbook.

If infra can support a pre-wired ephemeral burst pool (8 slots) that maps 1:1 to the pilot buffer, product will expose a toggle in the Dedicated UI for enabling the pilot mode and mark routes for fallback. Marcus, can you confirm technical constraints here?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product — Dedicated

Subject: Re: Pilot buffer policy and temporary burst-lane coordination

Marissa / Kim / Laura,

Thanks — tagging technical constraints and a pragmatic approach. TL;DR: we can do an ephemeral burst lane but cannot dynamically exceed cluster-level hard limits without manual provisioning; recommended approach below.

Constraints:
- Physical cluster capacity: current cluster utilization by region-west sits at ~78%. We have headroom for a small ephemeral carve (8 slots) only if we re-schedule non-critical background batch jobs or shift a host to the dedicated cluster for the pilot window.
- Autoscale controls: the runtime supports tenant-scoped soft_limits and hard_limits. Soft_limits can be raised per-tenant by policy; hard_limits require operator action.

Recommended implementation (fastest, lowest risk):
1) Create an ephemeral burst pool (8 slots) pre-provisioned on a small host group and tagged to Nimbus pilot. This pool is separate from default tenant pool and billed to Nimbus at pilot rates.
2) Implement a scheduled eviction hook: at 23:45 local time runbook triggers immediate rejection of new burst requests and sets pool to drain; at 00:15 purge remaining spot allocations and return host to general pool.
3) Manual approval path: If the ephemeral pool is under pressure, oncall is notified and can escalate to add one extra host (subject to finance sign-off for overage).

I'll open JIRA-OPS-1298 with the provisioning steps and a minimal runbook. I also pushed a stub to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pilot-capacity (contains proposed cluster assignment + Excel).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra — Serving Runtime

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks — procurement side at Nimbus here. A couple of quick items from legal/billing: 
- We need the pilot carveout and billing attribution documented in an MSA amendment or a short SOW. Can you share the rates for the ephemeral burst pool?
- SLA ask: for pilot only we'll accept a soft latency SLO, but we need a fallback plan documented (if you will route to alternative model/region, we need to capture expected P95 changes).

If you can share the Excel and a brief amendment draft I can route internally and revert with sign-off timeline (likely 48–72 hours).

Nadia

Team / Nimbus,

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and confirmed next steps on our side: 
1) Infra will provision an ephemeral burst pool as described (Marcus will open JIRA-OPS-1298 and mark the provisioning task high priority).
2) Product (Kimberly) will add a pilot toggle in the Dedicated UI and wire route fallbacks; estimate: small UI flag + backend routing rule, target mid-week delivery.
3) Marissa will send a 1-page SOW amendment with hourly burst rates and pilot dates; Nimbus procurement to review (Nadia).
4) Ops runbook: Laura to draft minimal runbook (attached: burst_lane_runbook.md) — eviction schedule, contact matrix, and billing attribution steps.

Action owners / deadlines: Marcus (JIRA-OPS-1298) by Mon 02-Mar EOD; Kimberly (pilot toggle) by Wed 04-Mar EOD; Marissa (SOW) by Mon 02-Mar noon; Laura (runbook) by Tue 03-Mar EOD.

If Nimbus is okay with this path, we will treat the pilot buffer as a scoped procurement amendment and not a permanent quota bump. Marissa — once you send the SOW I'll queue in Legal for a short review.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
